nodes.name: Tool Call In
nodes.notes: The ONLY entry point, matching VIO-agent-tool-ask-human. There is deliberately no webhook: this workflow blocks on a human for as long as it takes, so an HTTP caller would time out at the proxy on a perfectly healthy run and be left unable to tell a timeout from a spend. Fewer entry points also means fewer paths to audit. Call it as a toolWorkflow v2.2 tool (toolHttpRequest cannot be an agent tool on this build).

nodes.name: Build Proposal (fail closed)
nodes.notes: Prices the plan from the actual lead list, never from the caller's claim, and refuses if it cannot state count, cost and the exact people. Cap is 10 — see the code comment for why that is below VIO-source-leads' free-search cap of 25.

nodes.name: Ask Human (wait)
nodes.notes: waitForSubWorkflow MUST stay true. With it false the parent races on without a decision and the reveal fires unapproved — it is the single parameter on this canvas whose quiet flip would defeat the whole gate, so test-reveal-gate.mjs asserts it. ask-human's trigger is inputSource:passthrough, so the whole item (query + plan) is handed over; its Shape Proposal reads .query and ignores the rest.

nodes.name: Verify Approval (fail closed)
nodes.notes: Re-derives the verdict instead of trusting the sub-workflow to have failed closed. Two facts must agree: approved === true AND outcome === "approve". If a genuine approval ever denies here, ask-human's output shape changed — fix the reader, never loosen the check.

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: Strict boolean equality — a string "true" cannot pass. Routing is only the FIRST of three gates: the false branch reports a refusal (it does not merely dead-end), and the true branch still lands on a node that re-checks the approval and throws.

nodes.name: Authorize Reveal (fail closed)
nodes.notes: The only node that can build an Apollo request. It THROWS on a non-approval rather than emitting zero items, re-reads the verdict from Verify Approval rather than trusting the IF, re-applies the cap at the point of spend, and re-checks the plan fingerprint the human was shown. It creates both apollo_url and apollo_body; the HTTP node has neither without it.

nodes.name: Apollo Reveal (people/match)
nodes.notes: POST https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/people/match — ONE LEAD CREDIT PER ITEM. The URL is an expression on purpose: there is no hardcoded endpoint here to fall back on, so a node rewired to feed this one without going through Authorize resolves the URL to undefined and fails before leaving the box. With no input items it does not execute at all. retryOnFail is deliberately NOT set: a retry is a second billable call. onError keeps one failure from hiding the other nine, and Collect turns it into a visible row.

nodes.name: Collect Reveals (no silent drops)
nodes.notes: Walks the AUTHORISED list, not the response list, so a lead Apollo never answered for becomes a row with status no_result instead of vanishing. Cost is reported as attempts, because Apollo bills the call, not the hit.

nodes.name: Denied Report
nodes.notes: The refusal branch. No credential, no request body, no edge to the Apollo node.

nodes.name: Report
nodes.notes: Single exit for both branches, and a narrowing one. Last node, so this is what the calling agent receives back from the tool.
